_meta.role: Developer Technology Engineer, AI - New College Graduate 2026

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on experience in CUDA kernel optimization and parallel computing performance engineering. Replaced TorchScript convolution layers with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing and constant memory and experience with 8-bit quantization for edge deployment. Strong background in C/C++, deep learning model optimization, and computer architecture from coursework in High Performance Architecture and Multiple Processor Systems.

experience.title: Research Fellowship
bullets: Trained U-Net segmentation with VGG-16, VGG-19, and ResNet-50 backbones on the BraTS 2020 multi-modal MRI dataset; evaluated on Dice Score and IoU, reporting accuracy-latency trade-offs for deployment.
Led a cross-cultural team of 7 as the sole ML-experienced student; took over as team lead mid-project to restructure task distribution and deliver the full pipeline within a 6-week window.

experience.title: AI/ML Intern
bullets: Fine-tuned DONUT, an OCR-free visual document understanding Transformer, on a custom medical billing dataset for structured field extraction using PyTorch and HuggingFace's VisionEncoderDecoder API.
Improved validation accuracy from 55% to 93% through improved preprocessing and model tuning.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Trained YOLOv8n on 1,133 annotated images achieving 83% mAP@50 on held-out validation; exported to ONNX and TFLite for optimized deployment.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Replaced TorchScript convolution layers in VGG16 with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing and constant memory for weights and biases, eliminating per-layer allocation overhead.
Coalesced kernel ran at 49.2ms vs. 73.3ms uncoalesced and 77.5ms CPU TorchScript baseline, a ~35% speedup with identical classification accuracy.

projects.name: MPI Hodgkin-Huxley Neuron Simulation
bullets: Implemented distributed dendrite computations across MPI workers with synchronous soma updates on a SLURM-managed cluster.
Achieved up to 10.49x speedup with 12 slave processes; characterized scaling behavior across dendrite counts and compartment depths.

projects.name: Parallel Ray Tracer with MPI Task Scheduling
bullets: Implemented and benchmarked four parallel work distribution strategies (static strip/block/cyclic, dynamic task queue) for rendering 5000x5000 pixel scenes using MPI.
Achieved up to 30x speedup with static strip partitioning across 55 processes; demonstrated dynamic task queue outperformed all static methods under unpredictable workloads.

projects.name: SLM Compression and Benchmarking for Edge Deployment
bullets: Reduced GPU memory footprint by ~55% via 8-bit quantization (bitsandbytes LLM.int8()) on TinyLlama 1.1B; profiled peak VRAM and inference latency using pynvml and psutil.
Benchmarked across HellaSwag, GSM8K, and ARC with <1% accuracy degradation, demonstrating near-lossless compression for edge deployment.
